description:
Data Standardizer provides implementations of various internationally recognised standards in data processing, covering topics ranging from languages to currencies and geographical entities. With strongly-typed enumerations for each standard (where applicable) or other targeted data types, you can represent these elements in your code such that errors with invalid values are minimised.

Provides types supporting communication-related standards, including:
- ITU-T E.164 telephony numbers
- MIME: media types, transfer encodings, base64 and quoted-printable codecs, character sets, data: URIs, encoded words and RFC 2231 parameter values
releaseNotes:
Breaking changes:
- A parameter given both as `name` and in an RFC 2231 form such as `name*` is now rejected as a duplicate (RFC 6838 §4.3), where the RFC 2231 value used to be kept.
- `MimeParameter.Equals` and `GetHashCode` compare the character set of such a value, so the same octets in different character sets are no longer equal.
- An encoded word in a character set that switches modes, such as ISO-2022-JP, is accepted only if it switches back to ASCII by its end (RFC 2047 §3), on every target and with every option.
- In `MimeQuotedPrintableMode.Body`, the quoted-printable decoder rejects an encoded line longer than 76 characters, not counting its transport padding and CRLF (RFC 2045 §6.7 rule 5).
- The quoted-printable encoder writes a bare LF in text as `=0A`, not as a CRLF line break, so the encoded data decodes to the original octets (RFC 2045 §6.7 rule 4).
- In a comment (`MimeEncodedWordContext.Comment`, `MimeQuotedPrintableMode.EncodedWordComment`), "Q"-encoded text containing a literal `\` is now rejected, as RFC 2047 §5(2) erratum 504 requires.
- `MimeCharsetResolver` no longer resolves charset names that aren't registered with IANA, such as `ascii`, `ucs-2`, `unicode` and `unicodeFFFE`; pass a resolver for them to the `MimeCharsetResolver` constructor to accept them.
- A Content-Transfer-Encoding mechanism that is neither one of the five RFC 2045 defines nor an x- token, such as uuencode or x-, is rejected as RFC 2045 §6.1 requires: MimeTransferEncoding.Parse and TryParse fail, and readers that parse the field report it as invalid.
- MimeEncodedWord.TryParse with AllowLongWords rejects a word over 75 characters that can't be written back within the limit: one with empty text, a language over 61 characters, or a character set the resolver doesn't resolve.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.Parse` and `TryParse` reject a number with any character between its digits, such as `1-205-555-0199`, whatever the `ItuE164InternationalNumberStyles`; remove any grouping before parsing.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.CreateNumberForNetwork(countryCode, identificationCode, subscriberNumber)` throws `ArgumentException` for an Identification Code not assigned under the Country Code, such as `IC110` (883) with `GMSS` (881).
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.Parse` and `TryParse` throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for a `numberStyles` value with a bit that no `ItuE164InternationalNumberStyles` member defines.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.ToString` and `TelephonyInfo` formatting throw `FormatException` for a pattern without a placeholder for every digit of the number, instead of dropping digits.

New:
- `MimeQuotedPrintableDecoderOptions.AllowLongLines` accepts quoted-printable lines longer than 76 characters (RFC 2045 §6.7 note 5).

Fixed:
- The package now includes its XML documentation, so IntelliSense shows member descriptions.
- `MimeCharsetResolver` returns a new instance of a built-in encoding on each call, so a caller that changes its `EncoderFallback` or `DecoderFallback` no longer changes the encoding other callers get.
- `MimeDataUri.TryParse` no longer treats a percent-encoded `/`, `;` or `=` in the media type as a delimiter (RFC 2397 §3).
- `MimeDataUri.TryParse` accepts type, subtype and parameter names that are RFC 2045 tokens, such as `text/x-a~b`, so it reads everything `MimeDataUri.Create` writes.
- `MimeDataUri.Create` percent-encodes `/`, `;` and `=` in a quoted parameter value.
- A `MimeParameter` read with `MimeMediaTypeParseOptions.AllowUnknownCharsets` in a character set that couldn't be resolved is written back as its octets in that character set (`UNKNOWN-8BIT` when it gave none), not as different text labelled UTF-8.
- The netstandard1.1 build decodes runtime and custom character sets as the other builds do: invalid octets become U+FFFD with `AllowInvalidOctets`, and valid ISO-2022-JP values are accepted.
- `Encoder.Convert` and `Decoder.Convert` of the built-in encodings accept empty input, and the netstandard1.1 `UTF-32` decoder fits the array `GetMaxCharCount` sizes.
- On netstandard2.0, `ISO-8859-1` from `MimeCharsetResolver` uses the caller's fallbacks, and `UTF-16` and `UTF-32` have a `BodyName` and `HeaderName`.
- The quoted-printable decoder removes trailing spaces and tabs (transport padding) of any length, instead of rejecting a run of more than 76 before a line break.
- In a comment, a "Q"-encoded word may now contain a literal double quote, and one is written as itself rather than as `=22` (RFC 2047 §5(2) erratum 504).
- `MimeEncodedWord.DecodeText` with `AllowSplitCharacters` reads a character split between words in the byte order that a byte order mark earlier in the run gives, and in the mode an ISO-2022 character set such as ISO-2022-JP is in at the end of the word before.
- "Q"-encoded words (`MimeEncodedWord`, and the "Q" modes of `MimeQuotedPrintable`) accept lower-case hexadecimal digits such as `=c3=a9` by default, which RFC 2047 §4.2 allows.
- `MimeMediaType` accepts lower-case hexadecimal digits in RFC 2231 extended parameter values, such as `%c3%a9`, by default (RFC 2231 §7, RFC 822 §2.1).
- `MimeCharsetResolver` reads `ISO-10646-UCS-2` and `csUnicode` as big-endian and holds them to the Basic Multilingual Plane, as the IANA registry requires, instead of reading them as little-endian UTF-16.
- `MimeCharset.TryGetDefault` gives `UTF-8` for `text/csv`, `text/turtle`, `text/vtt`, `text/javascript` and `text/ecmascript`, and no default for `text/xml-external-parsed-entity`, as their registrations say.
- Quoted parameter values accept the US-ASCII control characters that RFC 822 allows, as text or as quoted-pairs, instead of rejecting them.
- `MimeMediaType.Tree` reports `Standards`, not `Unregistered`, for subtypes that start with `x-`, such as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (RFC 6838 §3.4).
- `MimeMediaTypeParseOptions.AllowQuotedExtendedValues` accepts an apostrophe in the value, as its docs say.
- `default(MimeParameter).TryFormat` and `FormatSections` no longer throw.
- `MimeEncodedWord` no longer writes a word longer than 75 characters, accepted with `MimeEncodedWordParseOptions.AllowLongWords`; its text is written as encoded words within the RFC 2047 §2 limit.
- MimeBase64Encoder in MIME mode makes progress with a destination of 4 or 5 characters at the end of a line.
- `MimeMediaType` compares the `access-type` and `permission` values of `message/external-body` without regard to case, and `mode` too when the access-type is `ftp`, `anon-ftp` or `tftp` (RFC 2046 §5.2.3).
- `MimeCharset.TryGetDefault` returns `false` for a `text` subtype with the `+xml` suffix, such as `text/foo+xml`, which has no default character set (RFC 7303 §4.2), instead of giving `US-ASCII`.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.Parse`, `TryParse` and `CreateNumberForNetwork(ulong)` accept a network number whose Subscriber Number has one digit, such as `+88165`.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.TryParse` returns `false` for a `null` string instead of throwing, and `Parse` names the parameter `s` when it throws `ArgumentNullException`.
- A new `ItuE164InternationalNumberFormatInfo` has the invariant patterns, so the `i` and `I` formats no longer give an empty string, and setting either pattern to `null` throws `ArgumentNullException`.
- With `TelephonyInfo` as the format provider, `string.Format` formats arguments that aren't E.164 numbers with the current culture.
- `TelephonyInfo` takes the neutral number patterns from the invariant culture, not the current UI culture.
- ItuE164InternationalNumber.TryParse returns false for a number with decimal digits other than 0-9.

Deprecated and removed:
- `MimeMediaTypeParseOptions.AllowLowercaseHexDigits` and `MimeEncodedWordParseOptions.AllowLowercaseHexDigits` are obsolete and have no effect, as lower-case hexadecimal digits are always accepted; they will be removed in a future major version.
